history: Designed after E6c showed exact-count and Bernstein decisions coincide when calibrated to the same bad-positive threshold. This follow-up changes how a fixed total confidence budget is distributed across policies, rather than renaming a confidence bound. Fresh seeds fixed before outcomes.
allocation: alpha_j = alpha * B_j^(-p) / sum_l B_l^(-p), where B_j=2*policy amplitude is fixed before rewards. p=1 primary and p=2 secondary. Exact binomial gate uses each candidate's own alpha_j and the same corruption correction. Uniform gives alpha/2 to both. The matched-risk control gives both policies the p1 bad-policy allocation, using oracle identity only to define an evaluation comparator; it is not a deployable generic tuning rule.
success: Higher mean utility with paired 95% interval excluding zero versus uniform at the same total alpha; no increase in empirical harm and strictly lower model-specific upper bound for the harmful candidate. Also compare uniform calibrated to the same harmful-candidate bound. Report the full grid, especially the reversed influence setting (good amplitude .45, bad .05). Do not claim global domination if this stress test fails.
validity: Allocation depends only on fixed policy coefficients, not evaluation rewards or true utility. Sum alpha_j=alpha; simultaneous lower confidence coverage remains at least 1-alpha. The exact adaptive endpoint attack and its checks are unchanged.
limits: Weighted Bonferroni allocation is established statistics. This is a proposed project-specific method and empirical mechanism study; novelty is unverified. A useful general method must choose allocations without assuming the low-influence candidate is the good one.
